example.question: How did DHL Group's consolidated net debt change in fiscal year 2025, and, according to the management report's discussion of the balance sheet (balance-sheet financial liabilities, not the net-debt table), which financing transactions were the main drivers of the increase in financial liabilities?
example.reference_answer: Net debt increased by €2,518 million, from €18,998 million at December 31, 2024 to €21,516 million at December 31, 2025. Balance-sheet financial liabilities rose from €24,209 million to €27,489 million (this differs from the €26,583 million 'financial liabilities' subtotal in the net-debt table, which excludes operating items), mainly because of bonds placed during 2025 with a total principal of €4.5 billion; the repayment of the 2017/2025 convertible bond (€1.0 billion) had an opposite effect.

evidence.text: Financial liabilities increased from €24,209 million to €27,489 million. The bonds placed over the course of 2025 with a total principal of €4.5 billion played a significant part in this. Repayment of the convertible bond 2017/2025 had an opposite effect of €1.0 billion.
Our net debt increased from €18,998 million as of December 31, 2024, to €21,516 million as of December 31, 2025.

example.question: What was DHL Group's consolidated profit before income taxes for fiscal year 2024 as originally reported in the 2024 annual report, does the 2025 annual report show the same comparative figure, and what was the FY2025 amount?
example.reference_answer: The 2024 annual report reports FY2024 profit before income taxes of €5,063 million. The 2025 annual report shows the FY2024 comparative as €5,062 million, i.e. €1 million lower. The difference stems from the commercial rounding introduced from fiscal year 2025 (prior-year figures were adjusted accordingly; apart from rounding there were no adjustments to prior-year figures). FY2025 profit before income taxes was €5,246 million.

evidence.text:
Starting from the 2025 fiscal year, the figures in this and other documents are commercially rounded. This means that the individual figures may not add up exactly to the total, and percentages may not exactly correspond to the figures shown. The prior-
year figures have been adjusted accordingly.
With the exception of the rounding differences described in note 1, there were no adjustments to prior-year figures in the 2025 fiscal year.
